Modal also offers a HIPAA BAA on its Enterprise plan (modal.com/blog/hipaa) — relevant context but not a dropdown option. Playbook rule: do not assert SOC 2 unless the report is on file in Vanta — Modal is not in scope.yaml and has no soc2_on_file_in_vanta attestation, so check Vanta / obtain the report via trust.modal.com before this dropdown is filled.

3.1.1.locator: Security and privacy at Modal (docs): 'All user data is encrypted in transit ... All public Modal APIs use TLS 1.3, the latest and safest version of the TLS protocol'; the same page states Modal forces HTTPS for all services using TLS
3.1.1.notes: Snippet-sourced (direct fetch blocked; an empirical TLS handshake against api.modal.com was impossible because the gateway blocks CONNECT). The claim covers 'all public Modal APIs'; whether TLS 1.3 (vs 1.2) is also the minimum for web endpoints serving Modal Functions and for internal service-to-service traffic is not stated in retrieved snippets — confirm with vendor before relying on '1.3' for the entire data path.

3.1.2.notes: Encryption at rest IS documented — modal.com/docs/guide/security: 'All user data is encrypted in transit and at rest' and 'Function inputs and outputs are stored encrypted at rest' — but no Modal page retrieved this session names the algorithm/standard (AES-128/256 etc.). A domain-restricted search for 'AES' on modal.com returned no algorithm statement. Writing 'AES-256' would be inference from industry norm, which the hard rules forbid; the honest dropdown value is 'Not known' with the positive encrypted-at-rest fact carried in 3.1.8. Searched: modal.com/docs/guide/security, /docs/guide/secrets, /docs/guide/customer-supplied-encryption-keys, /legal/dpa (all via snippets; direct fetches blocked).

3.1.3.notes: Backup encryption is not documented separately anywhere on Modal's public pages retrieved this session ('Not known' is the playbook-expected answer here). Related mitigating controls found instead: function inputs and outputs are deleted within a maximum TTL of 7 days (small payloads ≤2 MiB inline in the metadata store, larger in object storage), and Modal Inference endpoints are zero-data-retention — request/response payloads are never written to disk (modal.com/docs/guide/security). Ask the vendor whether customer data appears in backups at all and, if so, how backups are encrypted.

3.1.4.locator: Customer Supplied Encryption Keys (docs): 'CSEK lets you provide your own key material when creating supported Modal resources, and Modal uses the key as part of the resource encryption flow, but does not persist the key' (key material 16–512 bytes) — framing that establishes the default (non-CSEK) flow uses Modal-provided keys
3.1.4.notes: Playbook default for managed cloud applied ('Key generated by Subprocessor (not customer-specific)' unless Tavus uses CMEK/BYOK — CHECK WITH THE HUMAN). Modal-managed default keys are implied by the CSEK page (customer keys are the opt-in exception), but Modal does not publicly document whether default at-rest keys are per-customer or shared, so the '(not customer-specific)' half is the playbook default, not vendor evidence. If Tavus supplies CSEK key material for the resources Modal processes, the correct dropdown becomes 'Key generated by your company'. Confirm both points (default key scoping; whether Tavus uses CSEK) before filling.

3.1.6.notes: No primary source states Modal can anonymize customer personal data on the customer's instruction. Adjacent-but-different fact found (do not conflate): the Terms of Service (October 2025 version) let Modal use 'Aggregated De-identified Data' — data collected in connection with Customer's use of the Service, in aggregate de-identified form, explicitly EXCLUDING Customer Data uploaded or submitted by Customer — for Modal's own business purposes. That is Modal de-identifying its own usage analytics, not a processor anonymization capability offered over SAP/Tavus personal data. Searched modal.com legal pages and docs via domain-restricted search.

3.1.7.notes: No mention of a pseudonymization capability anywhere in retrieved Modal material. The DPA commits to 'appropriate technical and organizational measures described on Schedule 2, including measures referred to in Article 32(1) of the GDPR' (modal.com/legal/dpa) — Art. 32(1)(a) names pseudonymisation, but Schedule 2's actual contents could not be retrieved this session, so no capability can be asserted. Ask the vendor for Schedule 2 of the DPA.

3.1.8.value:
All user data encrypted in transit and at rest; all public Modal APIs use TLS 1.3 and HTTPS is forced for all services
Compute jobs containerized and virtualized with gVisor (Google's sandboxing container runtime, as used in Google Cloud Run/GKE), with syscall-filtering logic isolating workloads from host OS and from other tenants
Data minimization: function inputs/outputs stored encrypted and deleted within a maximum TTL of 7 days; Modal Inference endpoints are zero-data-retention (payloads never written to disk, in-flight network traffic only)
Secrets stored as encrypted objects until container startup
Customer Supplied Encryption Keys (CSEK) available for supported resources — Modal uses customer key material in the encryption flow and does not persist the key
Least-privileged approach to customer data: Modal states it will never access or use customer source code, function inputs/outputs, or anything stored in Images and Volumes
External penetration testing firms engaged to assess software security; internal code reviews via PR-based development workflow (GitHub)
Region selection incl. EU-only execution (region="eu" pins Functions/Sandboxes to EU datacenters)
Role-based access for service users (Viewer/Contributor per Environment) with production isolated from dev/staging
SOC 2 Type II audit completed, report available via Security Portal (trust.modal.com); HIPAA BAA available on Enterprise plan
3.1.8.locator: Assembled one-per-line from: docs/guide/security (encryption in transit/at rest, TLS 1.3, gVisor, 7-day TTL, zero-data-retention inference, least-privileged access, pen testing, PR-based review, SOC 2), docs/guide/secrets (encrypted secret objects), docs/guide/customer-supplied-encryption-keys (CSEK), docs/guide/region-selection (EU pinning), docs/guide/service-users (RBAC/least privilege), blog/hipaa (BAA), blog/soc2type2 (SOC 2 Type II)
3.1.8.notes: Every line traces to a modal.com page surfaced in domain-restricted search snippets this session; none of the pages could be fetched directly (gateway 403). open_questions_for_vendor: Please provide the full registered/mailing address of Modal Labs, Inc. (none is published on modal.com's legal pages), and confirm the exact legal entity and state of incorporation (Delaware corporation?) that contracts for the service Tavus uses.
Has Modal Labs, Inc. designated a representative in the EU under Article 27 GDPR? If yes, please provide the representative's name and full address.

Does Modal have a formally appointed Data Protection Officer? If yes, please provide name, telephone number and/or email; if not, please confirm security@modal.com (or another address) as the contact entitled to respond to data-protection requests, plus a telephone number if available.

Your docs state all user data is encrypted at rest — which algorithm/standard is used (e.g. AES-256), for (a) function inputs/outputs, (b) Volumes/Images, (c) the metadata store, and (d) object storage?
Are backups taken of customer data, and if so are they encrypted and with which algorithm?

Can Modal anonymize and/or pseudonymize customer personal data on the customer's documented instruction (Art. 28(3)(e) GDPR support), as distinct from the 'Aggregated De-identified Data' usage-analytics right in your Terms of Service? Please also provide Schedule 2 (TOMs) of your DPA.
Please provide your current SOC 2 Type II report (via trust.modal.com) and confirm whether Modal holds any ISO certifications (27001/27018/27701/9001/22301) — none are claimed on your public pages.

Does the EU region offering (region="eu") cover the full processing chain for real-time video/audio inference workloads — container execution, input/output routing (routing_region), Volumes/object storage, and control-plane metadata — such that personal data can be kept within the EU/EEA end to end?
